examples.name: A new user can sign in and register for multi-factor authentication.
examples.methodology: This example does not run. If promoted, the browser and application flow would be real: the test would create a new account through the user interface, enroll an authenticator second factor, sign out, and sign back in with the password plus a current authenticator code before observing the account page. The identity backend would need an isolated test tenant or emulator, the authenticator-code helper would be test-only, and authentication responses would not be mocked. SMS and email enrollment are not covered.

examples.name: Signing in with a wrong password shows an error and does not open the account.
examples.methodology: This example does not run. If promoted, it would use the real browser and application flow with an isolated test account to submit a known wrong password, observe the visible error, verify that account navigation and multi-factor enrollment do not appear, then visit the protected account URL directly and observe the sign-in page instead of account content. The account credentials would be test-only, and authentication responses would not be mocked. This checks browser-observable access and does not inspect the identity provider's internal session storage.

examples.name: Water depth in meters equals the surveyed water elevation minus the surveyed bed elevation.
examples.methodology: This example does not run. If promoted, it would call the real production water-depth calculation through an imported production seam and compare exact known surveyed values: 103.75 m water minus 101.25 m bed equals 2.5 m, and 99.5 m water minus 100 m bed equals -0.5 m. Inputs are fixed test values; no calculation or response is mocked. It does not read a map or network response.

tests.name: Open the page on water for the Jalama Near Lompoc gauge Creek Segment only, with the camera framed there and no leftover synthetic ribbons.
tests.methodology: Opens the locally served page and waits until the read-only test seam reports ready. The browser page, ArcGIS SceneView, and committed published creek data are real. Esri World Imagery and Esri World Elevation responses are real and are reused from a local disk cache; a response missing from the cache is fetched live, and if that fetch is unavailable the result is inconclusive rather than passed. Nothing else is mocked. The test-only seam supplies the water-segment list, water-graphic identity, and camera target. The test checks that only Creek Segment 27714637-026 has water, that exactly one water graphic exists for that segment, that the camera target is within 300 m of that segment's midpoint from the committed path, and that the removed synthetic controls are absent. It does not check the visual appearance of the water.

tests.methodology: Starts from the opening observation, then sets the real time slider to the published 2026-01-03T15:15Z flood peak and checks that the selected time and water-bucket identity change while exactly one water graphic remains on Creek Segment 27714637-026. The browser page and committed published data are real. Esri World Imagery and Esri World Elevation responses are real and are reused from a local disk cache; a response missing from the cache is fetched live, and if that fetch is unavailable the result is inconclusive rather than passed. Nothing else is mocked. It does not check the visual appearance of the water.

tests.methodology: Scrubs the real time slider to a mid-record observation taken from the committed series, presses the Play button, and samples the selected time until the samples have moved forward by 15-minute steps, then presses Pause and checks that the time stays unchanged for 1 second. The browser page and committed published data are real. Esri World Imagery and Esri World Elevation responses are real and are reused from a local disk cache; a response missing from the cache is fetched live, and if that fetch is unavailable the result is inconclusive rather than passed. Nothing else is mocked. It does not check the visual appearance of the water.

tests.name: Select a Jalama gauge time with no observation and show no water on its Creek Segment.

It checks that the water-segment list is empty and that the status "No observation at this time" is visible in both cases. The browser page and committed published data are real. Esri World Imagery and Esri World Elevation responses are real and are reused from a local disk cache; a response missing from the cache is fetched live, and if that fetch is unavailable the result is inconclusive rather than passed. tests.name: Hide every numeric water-surface elevation, stage, and discharge value on the page.
tests.methodology: At the opening time, the published flood peak, and a gap slot, reads document.body.innerText plus every aria-label, aria-valuetext, and title value and checks that none contain a water number, the words stage or discharge, or the published water-surface elevations for those times rounded to 1, 2, or 3 decimals. The browser page and committed published data are real. Esri World Imagery and Esri World Elevation responses are real and are reused from a local disk cache; a response missing from the cache is fetched live, and if that fetch is unavailable the result is inconclusive rather than passed. Nothing else is mocked. Console output and the visual appearance of the water are not checked.

enforcementChange.reason: Product direction reversed: the Experience now shows water-surface elevation, stage, and discharge values rather than hiding them. The test's forbidden-numbers rule contradicts the current intended behavior.

enforcementChange.approvalEvidence: Developer approved retirement on 2026-10-15 in the governance housekeeping task that accompanied this catalog change.

tests.name: Zoom out from the Jalama Creek Segment without exposing an empty flat-color coastal void.
tests.methodology: Opens the locally served page in test mode and waits until the test seam reports ready and SceneView has finished loading with a still camera. The browser page, ArcGIS SceneView, and committed published creek data are real. Esri World Imagery and Esri World Elevation responses are real and are reused from a local disk cache; a response missing from the cache is fetched live and saved. When a live fetch fails with DNS, TLS, HTTP 429, or HTTP 5xx and no frame failed, or no terrain tiles arrive, the result is inconclusive rather than passed. Nothing else is mocked. After the opening frame, the test-mode camera command moves the camera instantly to a fixed coast-scale pose about 12 km up, the pose three mouse-wheel notches reach, and waits again until the scene has finished loading. At the opening frame and the coast frame it screenshots a 640×480 clip of the scene, masks the sidebar using its DOM bounding box, samples every fourth pixel, and fails when the share of those pixels whose RGB exactly equals the single most common RGB exceeds 10%. A measured flat-color failure stays a failure even when Esri also reported an outage. The failure names the step, camera height, flat color, and share, and attaches the screenshot. It does not check mouse-wheel input, intermediate zoom levels, a white far-zoom frame, imagery sharpness, tile vintage differences, terrain accuracy, or water appearance.
tests.rootCauseAnalysis: Symptom: zooming out from the Jalama Creek Segment exposes an empty flat-color coastal void. Root cause: old USGSImageryOnly transparent coastal tiles let the navy ground color show through. Red evidence: commit cac781c measured 34% flat navy in the optimized crop; fixed coast frames stay at or below 4.4%. Fix: Esri World Imagery replaces those transparent coastal tiles. Future triage: if a coast frame is flat navy, inspect imagery tile transparency and ground show-through before treating the frame as an imagery outage.

tests.name: Zoom across the Jalama creek scene without raising tile-shaped terrain slabs.
tests.methodology: Opens the locally served page in test mode and waits until the test seam reports ready and SceneView has finished loading with a still camera. The browser page, ArcGIS SceneView, and committed published creek data are real. Esri World Imagery and Esri World Elevation responses are real and are reused from a local disk cache; a response missing from the cache is fetched live and saved. When a live fetch fails with DNS, TLS, HTTP 429, or HTTP 5xx and no frame failed, or no terrain tiles arrive, the result is inconclusive rather than passed. Nothing else is mocked. It checks three settled frames: the opening frame; the slab camera, where the old custom elevation layer drew 100% missed ground rays (camera at about -120.474, 34.502, 1,245 m up, heading 321°, tilt 58°); and a wide camera about 12 km up. The test-mode camera command moves the camera instantly to each fixed pose and the test waits until the scene has finished loading. Each frame samples an 8×8 grid in the central scene through sampleRenderedGroundHeights, which uses SceneView toMap on the drawn ground and not ground.queryElevation. The grid stays right of the sidebar and below the outer horizon band so the fixed Esri scene returns terrain hits. The test fails when more than 20% of those samples are null, when any non-null height is outside -20..2500 m, or when at least 6 edge-contiguous samples form a block whose elevation range is under 1 m, whose median is more than 120 m above the median of the adjacent ring, and whose samples span more than 200 m on the map. A measured terrain failure stays a failure even when Esri also reported an outage. Failure messages include the measured null share, heights, and plateau figures. It does not check mouse-wheel input, intermediate zoom levels, the return to the opening camera, exact terrain accuracy, imagery appearance, sharpness, vintage, ocean flatness, or water placement.
tests.bugReference: lifted tile-shaped terrain slabs during zoom
tests.rootCauseAnalysis: Symptom: a large photographic square appears lifted high with vertical walls during zoom. Root cause: old custom Usgs3DepElevationLayer.fetchTile returned a plain {values,width,height,noDataValue,usedMemory} object instead of new ElevationTileData(...); ArcGIS received undefined minValue/maxValue/hasNoDataValues, so terrain mesh bounds became invalid/NaN and tiles drew as vertical walls. Raw 3DEP heights were valid (about 0–330 m), so source-height queries false-passed. Reproduction baseline: git commit cac781c, old USGS scene, viewport 1440×900, wheel at (893,495), deltaY 420; by notch 3 the camera was about (-120.474, 34.502), z about 1245 m, heading 321°, tilt 58°; rendered view.toMap samples were 100% null while source elevation was 0–328 m. Fixed-environment evidence: returning actual ElevationTileData made samples 0% null at that camera; the current fix removes the custom layer and uses Esri World Elevation. Future failure triage: first inspect the rendered toMap hit rate and any custom ElevationLayer fetchTile return type or metadata; then inspect similar mesh-bound failures; only after that investigate source elevation values.

tests.name: Zoom far out from the Jalama Creek Segment and back in without the scene clearing to a flat white frame.
tests.methodology: Opens the locally served page in test mode and waits until the test seam reports ready and SceneView has finished loading with a still camera. The browser page, ArcGIS SceneView, and committed published creek data are real. Esri World Imagery and Esri World Elevation responses are real and are reused from a local disk cache; a response missing from the cache is fetched live and saved. When a live fetch fails with DNS, TLS, HTTP 429, or HTTP 5xx and no frame failed, or no terrain tiles arrive, the result is inconclusive rather than passed. Nothing else is mocked. After the opening frame, the test-mode camera command moves the camera instantly to a fixed far pose about 340 km up, then back to the opening camera, waiting each time until the scene has finished loading. At the opening frame, the far frame, and the return frame it screenshots a 640×480 clip of the scene, masks the sidebar using its DOM bounding box, samples every fourth pixel, and fails when the share of those pixels whose RGB exactly equals the single most common RGB exceeds 10%. It also fails when the far camera altitude is not above 100,000 m. A measured flat-color failure stays a failure even when Esri also reported an outage. It does not check mouse-wheel input, intermediate zoom levels, imagery sharpness, tile vintage differences, terrain accuracy, or water appearance.
tests.bugReference: far-zoom white scene caused by the local view far clip
tests.rootCauseAnalysis: Symptom: zooming far out clears the scene to an all-white frame, and zooming back in does not reliably recover it. Root cause: the old local SceneView constraints.clipDistance.far of 80000 cleared the frame once view rays exceeded the 80 km far clip. Red evidence: baseline commit cac781c; the optimized crop measured 92% flat white. Fix: a global SceneView with no 80 km far clip. Future triage: compare camera altitude with the view clipping constraints before investigating an imagery outage.

tests.name: Clicking the creek scene does not draw a (usually light blue) focus frame around the view.
tests.methodology: Loads the Esri dark theme and the app stylesheet, in that order, on a local page whose only view markup is an .esri-view containing a focusable .esri-view-surface. SceneView, the map, imagery, terrain, and the network are absent. The test clicks the surface and reads the computed outline of its ::after pseudo-element. It fails when that outline has a non-zero width and a painted style. It does not check keyboard focus, widget rings, water, or camera navigation.
tests.rootCauseAnalysis: Symptom: clicking the creek scene paints a light-blue frame around the whole view. Root cause: the Esri dark theme draws that frame on .esri-view .esri-view-surface:focus::after as a 2px solid Calcite brand outline, offset -2px. Calcite is Esri's design system. The surface is focusable, and its own outline is already 0, so resetting the element outline misses the frame. Reproduction: before the fix, the clicked surface ::after outline measured 2px solid rgb(0, 122, 194). Fix: the app stylesheet clears that ::after outline for pointer focus and leaves the keyboard :focus-visible ring. Future triage: after a click, inspect the surface ::after computed outline width, and confirm the app stylesheet still loads after the Esri theme.

tests.name: Looking up from below the water surface, the water-surface polygon fills the view and does not leave a hole exposing the bank terrain beyond.
tests.methodology: Opens the locally served page in test mode and waits until the test seam reports ready and SceneView has finished loading with a still camera. Pins Creek Segment 27714637-026's water-surface elevation to 26.50 m through the test seam, confirming via segmentPlacements that the active bucket's minimum reads 26.5 m. Moves the camera instantly to a fixed below-water, upward-looking pose at (-120.48482532, 34.51368790, 26.037 m), heading 342.70°, tilt 95.47°, and settles the scene. For each of a captured hole ground point and a captured known-good ground point on segment 27714637-026 at water-surface elevation 26.50 m, projects the WGS84 point to a screen pixel through the test seam and calls hitTestAtScreen on that pixel. The test fails when hit-testing either point returns no water-surface hit on segment 27714637-026, or when the returned bucket minimum is not 26.5 m. The browser page, ArcGIS SceneView, and committed published creek data are real. Esri World Imagery and Esri World Elevation responses are real and are reused from a local disk cache; a response missing from the cache is fetched live, and if that fetch is unavailable the result is inconclusive rather than passed. Nothing else is mocked. It does not check pixel color, polygon area, exact rim position, or the behavior of any other segment.
tests.bugReference: water-surface polygon rim leaves a hole exposing the bank terrain beyond
tests.rootCauseAnalysis: Symptom: at a below-water, upward-tilt camera over Jalama Creek, visible holes appear along the water-surface polygon rim; a view.hitTest through one of those holes returns zero water-surface hits and resolves on the bank terrain beyond. Root cause: 1 m USGS 3DEP cell quantization produces a stair-stepped waterline where the water surface meets the bank; without an outward dilation of the wet mask before the contour is traced, the polygon rim sits exactly on those raster cells, leaving sub-cell gaps between the polygon edge and the real bank. Low- and upward-tilt camera rays find those gaps. Red evidence (2026-10-15, segment 27714637-026 at WSE 26.50 m, camera -120.48482532, 34.51368790, 26.037 m, tilt 95.47°): hitTest at the hole ground point (-120.48485151, 34.51378253) returned hits=[]; at the adjacent known-good ground point (-120.48483593, 34.51372363, z 26.5) it returned one water-surface hit for segment 27714637-026 at bucket 26.5–26.55 m. Fix: BANK_OVERLAP_MARGIN_M = 2 in pipelines/creek-visualization-data-production/constants.ts dilates the wet mask by 2 cells before the contour is traced, bounded by the Creek Segment corridor so it cannot bleed into a neighbouring creek. Future triage: at a low- or upward-tilt camera over the creek, a hitTest returning zero water-surface hits on a pixel where a known-active segment should cover points first at the bank-overlap margin or the WSE publishing pipeline before anything else.

tests.name: Playing at 0.5×, 1×, 2×, 5×, and 10× advances the observation slider by about 5, 10, 20, 50, and 100 slots in one second.
tests.methodology: Opens the local page on the timeline fixture while the test server has VITE_TEST_MODE set. That path runs the real Play button, time slider, and speed buttons through the production timeline control, on a 500-slot stand-in clock. The ArcGIS scene, imagery, terrain, and published gauge series are not loaded, and the test fails if the page requests ArcGIS. For each of 0.5×, 1×, 2×, 5×, and 10×, the test pauses, returns the slider to the first slot, clicks that speed button, clicks Play, and reads the slider index at the start and end of one second inside the page. The slot count must sit within 10% of the target for that elapsed time, and the margin is never tighter than one slot, so 1× passes at 9–11 slots in one second. It does not check water, button highlight color, reverse playback, or a chosen calendar date.

tests.name: Highlight the current playback speed, starting at 1× until another speed is chosen.
tests.methodology: Opens the timeline fixture page, waits until the page stylesheet has painted, and reads the computed background, border, and text color of the five speed buttons. Before any click, 1× is the only button whose paint differs. It then clicks 2× and checks that 2× is the only button whose paint differs. The ArcGIS scene and published gauge series are not loaded. It does not press Play, and it does not check how fast the slider moves or the map.

tests.name: Open the Jalama time slider at the first observation slot, not the last.
tests.methodology: Opens the timeline-only page for the real published Jalama record and the app's real opening slot. The 3D scene is not loaded, and the test fails if the page requests ArcGIS. When the time readout leaves the loading text, the slider's slot is 0 and is before the last slot. It does not press Play, and it does not check water, playback speed, or the map.

tests.name: The catalog rejects a test entry that breaks the classification rules, and feature filters return each matching test once.
tests.methodology: Builds a sample catalog in memory, breaks one classification rule at a time, and checks that validation names that break, including a malformed catalog test identifier and a category prefix that does not match its category. It also checks that a feature filter returns each matching sample once, and that asking for one catalog test identifier still returns that test when it is disabled. With synthetic Playwright JSON, it checks that the stored result is the final attempt: a later pass after an earlier failure or inconclusive attempt is passed with a passed-after-retry record, a single pass has no flag, a final failure stays failed, and a final inconclusive attempt stays inconclusive. It does not open the catalog page, require the live catalog to contain zero tests, or run an application test. It checks that a Bug Check requires a nonempty bug reference and root cause analysis on a Feature Behavior Test, and that a baseline test leaves both null.

tests.name: The release check runs the core tests first and stops before feature tests if a core test fails.
tests.methodology: Calls the same release-gate function the release command uses, with stand-in results. It checks that core runs first and that a failing or inconclusive core result stops the feature phase. It does not run the application or a real failing core test.
